pine-needle.$description: Pine Needle — Major text and brand accents; a muted, verdant green providing organic warmth to headings and links.

powder-sand.$description: Powder Sand — Subtle surface backgrounds and highlights, giving a soft, natural base for UI elements.

lunar-dust.$description: Lunar Dust — Clean primary background, a slightly off-white that adds warmth without starkness.

white-linen.$description: White Linen — Secondary surface background, contrasts gently with Lunar Dust, also used for button text.

charcoal-bark.$description: Charcoal Bark — Primary text on light backgrounds and button fills; a very dark, desaturated gray that is softer than pure black.

deep-moss.$description: Deep Moss — Darkest text and background for high-contrast elements, subtly colored rather than truly black.

ash-grey.$description: Ash Grey — Subtle text and input colors for secondary information, providing clear readability without dominance.

pale-mauve.$description: Pale Mauve — Internal UI background for distinct sections, adding a touch of muted color.

sunken-orange.$description: Sunken Orange — Highlight accent color for specific textual elements, a warm pop of muted orange.

stone-grey.$description: Stone Grey — Disabled states for buttons and subtle border details.

shadow-tint.$description: Shadow Tint — Subtle, diffused shadows, almost a light beige, contributing to the soft, natural aesthetic.

simplon-norm.$description: Primary sans-serif for body text, navigation, and functional elements. Its range of weights and precise letter spacing ensures versatility from small captions to impactful headings.

saol.$description: Signature serif for headings, where its light 300 weight against typical heading sizes creates a sophisticated, understated elegance. The generous negative letter spacing further enhances its delicate appearance. This is a deliberate choice for authority through restraint.

simplon-mono.$description: Monospaced font for technical details or subtle accents, adding a touch of precision and contrast to the primary typefaces without being overly dominant. Its use is minimal.
